prompt: Problem 1 (Bone development & gymnastics). A study of 46 female subjects (GYM vs NON groups, the latter matched on age at menarche, size, physical maturity) with annual DXA scans; response is Sub-head bone mineral content (BMC), with covariates recorded at each scan. Acting as the analyst:
parts: 1. Is this a randomized experiment or an observational study? What is the treatment whose effect is studied?
2. Examine to what extent the matching covariates (age at menarche, standing height, FA length, Sub-Head LM) are balanced between NON and GYM. Summarize with tables/graphs (≤2 pages).
3. Perform exploratory analysis (summaries and plots, no modeling) of the association between gymnastics and bone development, with interpretation (≤2 pages).
4. Develop a model for the association between gymnastics and bone development, explaining your logic and interpreting parameters (iterative model building with diagnostics).
5. Provide a written assessment of the effect of gymnastics on bone development.
notes: Prof. Sijian Wang. Data-analysis problem; dataset not in repo. Transcribed from extracted text.
data: GYM VS NON (Excel) — not distributed with the SharePoint PDF download

prompt: Problem 2. Observe $Y = (y_1, y_2, y_3, y_4) \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(n; \frac{1+\theta}{3}, \frac{1-\theta}{3}, \frac{1-\theta}{3}, \frac{\theta}{3})$ with $n = 200$. Consider the augmentation $Z = (u_1, u_2, y_2, y_3, y_4)$ with $y_1 = u_1 + u_2$ and $Z \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(n; \frac13, \frac{\theta}{3}, \frac{1-\theta}{3}, \frac{1-\theta}{3}, \frac{\theta}{3})$.
parts: (i) Derive an EM algorithm based on this data augmentation to find the MLE $\hat\theta$.

(ii) With $p(y;\theta)$ the pmf of $Y$ and $f(z;\theta)$ that of $Z$, show $\frac{d^2}{d\theta^2}\log p(Y;\theta) = \mathbb{E}_\theta[\frac{d^2}{d\theta^2}\log p(Z;\theta)] + \operatorname{var}_\theta[\frac{d}{d\theta}\log p(Z;\theta)]$, the expectation/variance under the conditional distribution of $Z$ given $Y$.
(iii) Use (ii) to show the observed Fisher information, hence an estimate $\hat V$ of the asymptotic variance of $\hat\theta$, can be obtained from the EM output.
(iv) Implement the EM in R; report $\hat\theta \pm$ SE when $Y = (108, 31, 27, 34)$.
(v) Design and run a simulation (fixed $n$) to check (1) approximate normality of the MLE about the true $\theta$, and (2) that $\operatorname{var}(\hat\theta)$ is well estimated by $\hat V$.
notes: Prof. Zhiqiang Tan. Self-contained simulation problem. Transcribed from extracted text.
